human_tolerance.notes: 'With rare exceptions, the brown rat lives wherever humans live, particularly in urban areas'; a true omnivore that excavates burrows, climbs and swims, and is a major pest of stored food and structures.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Judgement. The article describes continuous breeding in warm, sheltered places such as sewers and buildings rather than a seasonal window, so the phase covers the whole year.

vocalizations.description: A dry, repeated squeak or shriek given when the rat is surprised or cornered, more often heard than seen; rats also hiss and grind their teeth when threatened.
A rapid, high-pitched chittering between individuals at a feeding or nesting site, including during courtship.

taxonomy.note: Rank, accepted name and authority from the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, which returns the scientific name 'Rattus norvegicus (Berkenhout, 1769)' and the order Rodentia for the genus Rattus.

external.note: GBIF usage key from the GBIF Backbone match for the scientific name; iNaturalist taxon id and Wikidata Q-id from Wikidata.

conservation.note: The article's taxobox gives the IUCN status as LC.

range.note: 'With rare exceptions, the brown rat lives wherever humans live' and it 'having become naturalised across the world'. The record marks Argentina as both native and introduced because the species is not native to the country but is established there; the native entry records the country in which the wild population lives, the introduced entry the fact that it is not actually native there. This is a schema-encoding judgement, not a claim that the rat is native to Argentina.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Brown rats dig well, and often excavate their own burrows' (Burrow), 'is a good swimmer, both on the surface and underwater' (Swim), and 'has been observed climbing slim round metal poles several feet in order to reach garden bird feeders' (Climb), on top of walking.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Not sourced. Judgement for a large rat, scaled from the stated head-and-body length of 15-28 cm and the described body build. This is an estimate, not a sourced figure.

traits.skin.note: 'The brown rat's fur is usually brown or dark grey, while the underparts are lighter grey or brown.'

traits.nest_type.note: 'Brown rats dig well, and often excavate their own burrows'; the species also shelters and nests in ground cavities and building voids. The schema's Burrow is the closest of its six nest types for a digging rodent.

traits.perching.note: The rat climbs poles and pipes but its posture and locomotion are terrestrial; the record does not treat it as a perching animal.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits 1.0 MamFuncDat row for Rattus norvegicus: BodyMass-Value 338.33 g, consistent with the article's 'Adult weight ranges from 140-500 g' and 'It is common for breeding wild brown rats to weigh less than 300 g'.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 'Adult weight ranges from 140-500 g.' The article adds that 'Large individuals can reach 800 g but are not expected outside of domestic specimens', which is why the field stops at 500 g.

traits.length_m.note: 'The head and body length ranges from 15-28 cm while the tail ranges in length from 10.5-24 cm'. Midpoint of the head-and-body range, 0.215 m; the tail is recorded separately through the look block's tail_ratio, matching how the schema's length_m is used elsewhere in the repository.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No open-licensed source gives a typical or maximum lifespan for Rattus norvegicus: the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles, Wikidata and GBIF carry none, and the field-guide and Animal Diversity Web pages were avoided under the licence policy. 3.0 years is a documented judgement placeholder for a wild rat, not a sourced figure.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits 1.0 MamFuncDat row for Rattus norvegicus: Diet-Inv 30, Diet-Fruit 20, Diet-Seed 40, Diet-PlantO 10 (Diet-PlantO is mapped to the schema's fruit share, giving 0.3 fruit in total). The article is consistent: 'It is a true omnivore and consumes almost anything, but cereals form a substantial part of its diet.'

traits.social.note: Brown rats live in groups in burrows and wall voids and forage in groups; group_size is a judgement for a typical commensal group.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'The brown rat is nocturnal and is a good swimmer.'

traits.defense.note: Authored: the rat drops from a perch, runs and hides into a burrow or crack when surprised, and bites if cornered, which the record encodes as Flee with the shriek carried as the alarm call.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from the species' nocturnal, light-avoiding behaviour and its readiness to bolt when disturbed.

habitat.use.note: 'With rare exceptions, the brown rat lives wherever humans live, particularly in urban areas' and it digs and excavates its own burrows; the 0.9/0.1 ground-heavy split is a judgement from that, since EltonTraits 1.0 carries no foraging-stratum fields for this species.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: 'Brown rats dig well, and often excavate their own burrows' - the rat rests and sleeps in its own burrows and in ground cavities.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow the EltonTraits diet shares; the burrow shelter weight of 0.9 reflects the described excavation, and compost stands for the scavenging the article describes at food waste and bins.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity, uses_gardens and light_max follow 'With rare exceptions, the brown rat lives wherever humans live, particularly in urban areas' and its nocturnal light-avoiding behaviour; road_mortality is judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: The rat is described as living wherever people do, in warm and sheltered ground-level habitats, with no migration or hibernation described.

seasonal.phases.note: The article describes continuous breeding in warm, sheltered places rather than a seasonal window; the phase dates are a judgement reflecting that.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The article gives no day counts for incubation, nestling or weaning; duration_days 40 and scale 0.55 are a documented judgement for a rodent's nestling and weaning period, not a sourced figure.

vocalizations.alarm.note: The article describes the species' vocalisations and its squeaking when surprised or cornered; the description is written from that account.

vocalizations.chitter.note: The article's account of groups foraging and interacting at feeding sites supports a contact call; the description is written from that account and no published description of the call was found.

look.note: 'The brown rat's fur is usually brown or dark grey, while the underparts are lighter grey or brown', with the long bare tail and pink feet the article describes alongside its good climbing and swimming. Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program: seed-based nocturnal foraging with a walking gait, the program's default sun window for a nocturnal species, and short flee and calm distances for a wary but habitat-tolerant commensal.
